title: Chat-first landing, unified users list, chat-request flow, and admin access separation

requirements.summary: Update post-login redirect logic to route unapproved users to /pending-approval and all approved users (including admin/super_admin) to /chat, never to /users based on role.
acceptanceCriteria: Given an unapproved user logs in or signs up, they are navigated to /pending-approval.
Given an approved normal user logs in or signs up, they are navigated to /chat.
Given an approved admin logs in or signs up, they are navigated to /chat.
Given an approved super_admin logs in or signs up, they are navigated to /chat.
No code path redirects users to /users based solely on role.

file_operations.description: Change redirect computation: if profile.approved === false -> /pending-approval; if approved === true -> always /chat regardless of role. Remove any role-based redirect to /users.
Update the onLoginSuccess route type to include /chat and ensure the login flow uses getPostLoginRoute() that now returns /chat for approved users.

Update the post-signup routing: first-user bootstrap (super_admin, approved) must navigate to /chat (not /users); all other new users remain /pending-approval. Preserve existing bootstrap logic (no role/approval changes beyond existing behavior).

requirements.summary: Make /chat the default landing for approved users and implement the Chat Home empty state with the exact text and a bottom-right FAB that navigates to /users.
acceptanceCriteria: When the current user has zero chats, /chat shows the empty-state text exactly: "Start a conversation. Tap + to find users."
A FAB is visible at bottom-right on /chat and uses a plus/new-chat icon.
Clicking the FAB navigates to /users.
Approved admin and approved super_admin users can access /chat and see the same chat home behavior as normal users.

file_operations.description: Remove the super_admin chat denial behavior so admin/super_admin can use normal chat flow. Replace the zero-chats UI with the required exact empty-state text and add a bottom-right FAB (use shadcn-ui Button + lucide-react plus/new-chat icon) that calls onNavigate('/users'). Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: Change /users into a single User List experience for all roles that lists all approved users including self, with avatar, name, and optional subtle role badge.
acceptanceCriteria: Navigating to /users shows a list of all approved user profiles returned by the data source, including admins and super_admins.
The currently authenticated user appears in the list.
Each list item shows avatar/photo and display name; role badge is present if implemented and is visually small/subtle.
/users no longer conditionally swaps to an admin-only user management screen based solely on role.

file_operations.description: Remove role-based swapping to UserManagementView; always render the unified ApprovedUsersListView for all roles (including admin/super_admin), keeping /users as the standard user browsing screen.

Update getApprovedUsers() to include the currently logged-in user (remove the exclusion filter) while continuing to only return users where approved == true. Ensure admins/super_admins are included when approved.

Update the user row UI to show profile photo (Avatar) and name prominently and add an optional small/subtle role badge (e.g., only when role != 'user') using shadcn-ui Badge. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: Adjust /users chat-request UX so tapping a user row does not open chat; instead it reveals a Send Chat Request action, writes a pending request record with correct semantics, and prevents duplicate pending requests.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking/tapping a user list row does not navigate to /chat and does not open an existing chat thread.
After selecting a user, the UI presents a "Send Chat Request" button to initiate a request.

Sending a request writes a Firestore document to the chat_requests collection (or existing chat request collection) with the correct semantics: requester as fromUid, recipient as toUid, status == "pending", and createdAt populated.
The app prevents duplicate pending requests from the same sender to the same recipient (either by UI state or backend rule), without deleting or modifying existing user documents.

file_operations.description: Change list interaction: clicking a user row should select/expand that row (or open an inline action area) instead of navigating to /chat. Show a "Send Chat Request" action only after selection. Remove the direct "Open Chat" navigation from the row tap path; keep any chat access only via accepted threads in /chat.

Update sendChatRequest() to enforce 'no duplicate pending requests' specifically (only block when a pending request already exists for the same sender/recipient). When creating a request, keep existing Firestore naming conventions for compatibility (e.g., fromUserId/toUserId used by security rules) but also include fromUid/toUid fields to match required semantics, with status = 'pending' and createdAt set.

requirements.summary: Ensure receivers see incoming pending chat requests, can accept/reject, and chats become visible/enabled for both users only after acceptance.
acceptanceCriteria: When User A sends a request to User B, User B sees an incoming request UI within the app without needing a manual refresh beyond existing polling behavior.
Accepting a request creates exactly one 1-to-1 chat thread containing both user IDs and allows both users to see/open it from /chat.
Rejecting a request updates the request status appropriately and does not create any chat thread.
Users cannot send messages to each other unless there is an accepted request/chat thread.

file_operations.description: Keep/adjust the incoming request polling UI so it clearly shows pending incoming requests with Accept/Reject actions. Ensure the UI uses existing polling behavior and updates list state after actions. Use shadcn-ui Card/Button patterns for consistent presentation. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Ensure /chat only lists actual chat threads (post-acceptance) and does not allow sending messages unless a chat thread exists/has been selected. Align any empty/loading states with the new chat-first landing behavior.

requirements.summary: Separate admin access from normal chat flow: admin dashboard is only reachable via header profile dropdown 'Admin Dashboard' for admin/super_admin, and admin screens are guarded without affecting /chat landing.
acceptanceCriteria: For a normal user, the header profile dropdown does not show any admin-only navigation items (including Admin Dashboard).
For an admin or super_admin, the header profile dropdown shows an "Admin Dashboard" item that navigates to the admin dashboard route.
Admin dashboard screens are guarded so only admin/super_admin can access them (direct navigation is blocked).
Approved admin/super_admin users still land on /chat after login and can use chat features without being redirected to admin areas.

file_operations.description: Replace the super_admin-only 'User Management' menu item with an admin/super_admin-only dropdown item labeled exactly "Admin Dashboard" that navigates to the admin dashboard route. Keep admin navigation out of normal users' menus. Use existing shadcn-ui DropdownMenu components. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Wire admin routes into the router (e.g., /admin and any existing admin subroutes used by the admin layout) and ensure they render the existing admin screens behind AdminRouteGuard. Ensure /chat remains the default post-login landing and no role-based redirect pushes users into admin routes.
Adjust unauthorized handling to navigate users back to /chat (not /home) and ensure guarded admin screens block direct navigation for non-admin users.
Update the onUnauthorized navigation target to /chat to match the chat-first flow and remove any coupling to non-existent or non-required routes.

requirements.summary: Enforce role/identity semantics: super_admin is both admin and a normal user for product behavior, included in user list and chat flow, without granting admin capabilities to normal users.
acceptanceCriteria: super_admin users can use /chat and /users the same way as normal users (subject to approval).
Admins and super_admins appear in /users like normal users (with optional role badge).
Normal users cannot access admin routes or see admin-only UI controls.

file_operations.description: Remove any role-based restriction that blocks super_admin/admin from chat, ensuring they use the same /chat experience as normal approved users.
Ensure /users is available for all roles and does not switch to admin-only management views based on super_admin role.
Ensure admin-only navigation is shown only for admin/super_admin and never for normal users, while not affecting access to /chat and /users.

requirements.summary: Meet safety constraints: avoid deleting user documents and avoid changing roles/approval flags as part of this update; preserve super_admin bootstrap behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: No migration or code path deletes user documents.
No migration or code path changes user.role or user.approved values as part of implementing the new flow (outside of existing explicit admin actions, if they remain available and guarded).
The first-user bootstrap behavior for super_admin remains unchanged.

file_operations.description: Remove or disable the "Delete User" action from the admin UI so there is no in-app code path that deletes user profile documents. Keep other explicit admin actions unchanged/guarded.
Remove the delete-user mutation wiring (and related export surface) so the frontend no longer invokes user-document deletion.
Stop passing any delete handler into row actions and ensure the admin users table no longer offers deletion from the UI.

requirements.summary: Apply a cohesive non-blue/non-purple theme across /chat and /users, consistent with Tailwind + shadcn, and ensure the FAB is prominent and accessible.
acceptanceCriteria: /chat and /users share a consistent visual style (typography, spacing, button styling).
The FAB meets basic accessibility expectations (keyboard focusable, visible contrast, clear hit area).

file_operations.description: Align spacing/typography with the rest of the app and ensure the FAB has a clear hit area, keyboard focus, and strong contrast using Tailwind + shadcn-ui Button styling. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Standardize cards, list rows, badges, and buttons to match the same non-blue/non-purple visual language as /chat (consistent spacing and hierarchy) using shadcn-ui components. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.
If needed, fine-tune existing CSS variables to reinforce a cohesive non-blue/non-purple palette across updated screens while preserving existing Tailwind token structure.
